cards.text: Grab your apron, friend. We're in First John, a letter written to believers, and John is going back to basics. He reminds them of the message they've heard from the very beginning: not new, not trendy, just the CLASSIC recipe.

cards.question: What's the message John's readers have heard from the beginning?

cards.text: John says don't be like Cain, Adam and Eve's son (Genesis 4:1), who belonged to the evil one and murdered his brother. Then John asks the big question himself: why'd Cain do it?

cards.question: John says Cain killed his brother because Cain's own deeds were ___, while his brother's deeds were ___.

cards.text: Then John turns to his readers and calls them brothers. He gives them a heads-up about how the world might treat them.

cards.question: True or false: John tells his brothers they should expect the world to love them.

cards.text: John says believers know they've passed from death to life. And he tells them EXACTLY how they know it.

cards.question: John says we know we've passed from death to life because we ___ our brothers.
True or false: John says the one who does not love remains in death.

cards.text: Then John swings right back around to Cain. He's got a word for anyone who hates his brother, and friend, it is not a soft word.

cards.question: What does John call everyone who hates his brother?

cards.text: And John says you know eternal life does not reside in a murderer. John is NOT sugarcoating this batch.
So what does real love actually look like? John says we can know it, and he points straight to Jesus.

cards.question: How does John say we know what love is?

answers.text: Jesus laid down His life for us
Jesus wrote it on stone tablets
Jesus showed it to us in a vision

cards.question: True or false: John says only Jesus was meant to lay down His life for others.

cards.text: Then John gets practical: picture someone with earthly possessions who sees his brother in need and withholds his compassion. That's me with a FULL cookie box, watching my friend go without, slowly closing the lid while we make eye contact.

cards.question: John asks a question about the person who sees his brother in need and won't show compassion. What does he ask?

answers.text: How can God's love abide in him
Why didn't his brother ask sooner
Who will pay his brother back

cards.text: Now John calls his readers little children and boils this whole thing down. Saying nice things is easy, so how should love really show up?

cards.question: How does John tell his little children to love?

cards.text: Not like the friend who texts "Let me know if you need anything!" and then on moving day his phone is off ALL DAY. John says loving in action and truth is how we'll know we belong to the truth.

cards.question: True or false: John says that by this we will also assure our hearts in His presence.

cards.text: But some days your own heart turns on you and points the finger. John says even if our hearts condemn us, there's something to remember about God.

cards.question: Even if our hearts condemn us, what does John say about God?

answers.text: God is greater than our hearts
God stays far from our hearts

cards.text: And He knows all things. Friend, my heart said a LOT about me back in that junk drawer, none of it nice, and God is greater than every single word of it.

cards.question: True or false: John says if our hearts do not condemn us, we should still be afraid before God.
John says we will receive from Him whatever we ask. Why?

answers.text: We keep His commandments and do what pleases Him
We ask Him again and again until He says yes
We give Him a tenth of everything we earn

cards.text: John keeps mentioning God's commandments. Now he spells out exactly what His commandment is, and it comes in two parts.

cards.question: His commandment is that we should ___ in the name of His Son, Jesus Christ, and ___ one another just as He commanded us.

cards.text: John says, "Whoever keeps His commandments remains in God, and God in him." Then he tells us how we can know He remains in us.

cards.question: How does John say we know He remains in us?

answers.text: By the Spirit He has given us
By the signs He shows us each day
By the dreams He gives us at night

findings.problem: John appears for the first time here ("John is going back to basics"), but the card never says who he is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card names John as the letter's writer. 1 John never names its author, so no verse can serve as the reference that facts from outside the passage need.
findings.question: For a letter that never names its author, like 1 John, may Papa Dorin name the traditional author (John) without a reference? Or should he call him something like "the writer" or "the apostle"?

findings.problem: "Then John swings right back around to Cain" says 1 John 3:15 is about Cain. The verse never mentions Cain, so the card makes a connection the text leaves open. It also all but hands the baker the answer to card 11 ("A murderer").

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "Saying nice things is easy, so how should love really show up?" rules out the wrong answer "In word and speech" on card 2 before the baker chooses.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The moving-day joke makes a made-up friend the one being laughed at, not Papa Dorin himself.

rule.text: Humble. When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself.

findings.problem: "By this" and "His presence" point back to things the question never states. The baker can't see the earlier card, so the question doesn't say what "this" is or whose presence it means.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "John keeps mentioning God's commandments" isn't true. Before this card the passage mentions commandments only once (1 John 3:22).

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: Blank 2 ("love" one another) asks again about "love one another," a line already asked about when it first appeared in 1 John 3:11 (stop 1, card 2).

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: Across the walkthrough, only three cards carry a real laugh (stop 1 card 16, stop 2 cards 3 and 7). Lines like "just the CLASSIC recipe" (stop 1 card 1) and "John is NOT sugarcoating this batch" (stop 1 card 12) read like a nice dad being pleasant, not laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
